Title: Project Engineering Manager, Staff
Industry: Semiconductor Manufacturing, Software Development, and Computer Hardware Manufacturing
Description:
We Are
  
  
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
  
  
What You'll Be Doing
  
  

* Own and maintain the integrated schedule and critical path across multiple Memory Interface IP development and release workstreams, from project kickoff and architecture through design closure, verification, customer delivery, and production readiness. Model dependency chains deeply enough to quantify the impact of slips and pull-ins, distinguish paths with float from those without it, and update the plan weekly using current engineering data.
* Drive the weekly project cadence by synthesizing inputs from architecture, RTL, design verification, analog and mixed-signal design, physical design, packaging, software, infrastructure, product engineering, and post-silicon teams into a single view of program health, emerging concerns, and required actions.
* Track verification convergence and engineering maturity as leading indicators. Monitor feature readiness, RTL closure, bug discovery and closure trends, regression health, coverage, design maturity, and block-level readiness. Recognize when convergence is stalling and drive a recovery plan before downstream milestones or customer commitments are affected.
* Analyze schedule scenarios and coordinate recovery plans. Work with engineering leads to understand technical constraints, resource limitations, and available float; quantify the impact of changes; develop practical options; and track agreed recovery actions to closure.
* Manage external partner and customer dependencies by owning delivery calendars, tracking execution plans and acceptance criteria, aligning technical dependencies, and supporting schedule negotiations with a clear understanding of downstream technical, commercial, and resource impacts.
* Lead cross-functional risk, issue, and decision management. Convert technical uncertainty into clear options, owners, dates, and decision points. Ensure risks, assumptions, and trade-offs are visible early and resolved at the appropriate level.
* Provide concise project insight to executives and customers. Distill complex engineering information into evidence-based updates that distinguish signal from noise, quantify schedule and delivery impact, and clearly identify the actions or decisions needed.

A Day In The Life
  
  
You start the morning reviewing verification-convergence dashboards and regression results, spotting a block where bug-closure velocity has slowed. You bring the DV lead and RTL owner together for a focused sync, clarify the cause, and align on a recovery plan before the weekly project review.
  
  
In that review, you walk leadership through an updated critical path that reflects an internal delivery shift, quantify the downstream impact on release timing and customer commitments, and identify the decisions needed to protect the plan. Later, you follow-up with R&D on the strategy to take to resolve the issue, then finish the day preparing a concise executive summary and following up on owners and due dates from the project review.
  
  
What You'll Need
  
  

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Applied Science, Computer Science, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience, with 8+ years of relevant experience in semiconductor, silicon IP, SoC, ASIC, or complex hardware development.
* Demonstrated experience managing complex semiconductor or silicon IP programs across multiple engineering disciplines and geographically distributed teams.
* Strong working knowledge of semiconductor development lifecycles and the relationships among architecture, RTL, verification, analog and mixed-signal design, physical design, software, infrastructure, and productization.
* Demonstrated ability to build and maintain integrated schedules with meaningful dependency and critical-path modeling, including float analysis, milestone confidence, and the downstream effects of schedule changes.
* Experience using engineering evidence such as feature readiness, bug trends, regression results, coverage, design closure, and delivery health to assess schedule risk and drive corrective action.
* Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate complex technical and program information, develop practical options, and recommend a course of action.
* Strong communication and influence skills, including the ability to gain cooperation across engineering teams, customers, suppliers, and external partners and to present crisp status and recommendations to senior leadership.
* Experience with project and program management tools and data-driven reporting. Familiarity with Jira, schedule-management tools, dashboards, and engineering lifecycle metrics is preferred.
* Knowledge of quality-management processes and the ability to navigate Linux environments are considered assets.

Who You Are
  
  
This is not a status-reporting role. You will connect a broad set of engineering workstreams into a coherent, dependency-driven plan, identify the real critical path week to week, and drive the cross-functional actions and decisions that keep complex Memory Interface IP projects on track. The work spans concurrent development efforts with significant interdependencies across engineering disciplines, customers, external partners, and development infrastructure.
  
  
Working with general direction, you will apply strong semiconductor-development knowledge and program-management judgment to analyze issues, recommend practical solutions, and gain cooperation across teams. Success requires attention to engineering detail, disciplined follow-through, and the ability to turn complex technical inputs into clear priorities, ownership, and delivery commitments.
  
  
The Team You'll Be Part Of
  
  
Our engineering teams develop advanced Memory Interface IP that enables customers to build high-performance, differentiated SoCs. We work at the intersection of architecture, analog and mixed-signal design, RTL, verification, physical design, software, infrastructure, and customer deployment. The programs are technically complex, globally distributed, and tightly connected to customer and business commitments.
  
  
We value people who combine advanced technical judgment with clear communication, disciplined execution, and the willingness to work through details without losing sight of the broader outcome. In this role, you will help shape how complex semiconductor programs are planned and delivered, strengthen execution practices across teams, and work alongside talented engineers solving consequential problems at scale.
  
  
Rewards and Benefits
  
  
We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

We are committed to provide access & opportunity to individuals with disabilities and will provide reasonable accommodation to individuals throughout the recruitment and employment process. Should you require an accommodation, please contact hr-help-canada@synopsys.com.

**Head of US Operational Technology**
=====================================

Every day, we deliver safe and secure energy to homes, communities, and businesses, connecting people to the energy they need for their lives. Our expertise and track record position us uniquely to shape the sustainable future of our industry as the pace of change accelerates. To succeed, we must anticipate customer needs, reduce energy delivery costs, and pioneer flexible energy systems. This requires delivering on our promises and seeking opportunities for growth.

In IT and Digital, we collaborate closely with the diverse energy businesses within the National Grid group, revolutionizing operations through technology. Embracing modern methodologies and digital mindsets, we drive efficiency and bring new capabilities to internal and external customers as we lead the charge toward a carbon-free future.

Our work is critical, as National Grid powers millions of homes and businesses across the UK and US, and the technology we employ is vital to this task. The successful applicant for this position will play a crucial role in our mission, supported by our multicultural, customer-centric global team, with opportunities for professional development.

**National Grid is hiring a Head of US Operational Technology role which operates under a hybrid working model and is open to candidates based at our Waltham, MA, Syracuse, NY, and Brooklyn, NY.**

**This is a hybrid role. Employees are expected to work from their assigned office or another approved work location outside the home at least three days per week. Additional in-person attendance may be required based on role, team, and business needs.**

### **Job Purpose**

The Head of U.S. Operational Technology (OT) is a senior leadership role accountable for the safe, reliable, resilient, secure and supportable operation of the technology environments that underpin real-time electric transmission, electric distribution and gas distribution operations across Massachusetts and New York. The role reports to the VP, Head of IT&D Electric and works in close partnership with Electric and Gas Operations, Cybersecurity, Engineering, Architecture, Regulatory, Capital Delivery and other enterprise technology leaders.

The role leads a multidisciplinary organization responsible for 24x7 operational support and lifecycle stewardship of OT applications and infrastructure. The scope includes Energy Management Systems (EMS), Gas Management System (GMS), Advanced Distribution Management Systems (ADMS), Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems (DERMS), SCADA-related capabilities and the supporting network, compute, storage, database, integration and recovery environments. It also includes designated technology supporting LNG operations, physical security systems, substation controllers and substation access points.

You’ll join an established team, building on its existing strengths to deliver meaningful outcomes. Working collaboratively with colleagues and stakeholders, you’ll help shape priorities, improve ways of working, and support the team’s continued development and success.

The Head of OT leads directors responsible for application and infrastructure domains and is a key partner to control center, operations, regulatory and executive stakeholders. The role requires experienced, visible leadership during significant events; disciplined governance; strong technical judgment; and the ability to convert technical risk into clear business decisions.

### **Key Accountabilities**

**Safe, Reliable and Resilient Operations**

* Own the availability, resilience, performance, and recoverability of the OT estate.
* Establish clear 24x7 operational accountability, escalation, and decision-making.
* Lead technology response to major incidents and operational events.
* Maintain and test business continuity, disaster recovery, and recovery capabilities.
* Ensure readiness for storms, grid emergencies, outages, and critical operational events.
* Drive continuous improvement through incident analysis and root-cause elimination.

**Cybersecurity, Safety, Compliance and Risk**

* Ensure readiness and compliance with applicable regulatory and cybersecurity requirements.
* Embed safety, cyber, compliance, and risk considerations into technology decisions.
* Maintain auditable controls, remediation plans, and risk management processes.
* Provide transparent reporting on operational, technology, and compliance risks.
* Support regulatory filings, rate cases, and investment planning.

**Technology Strategy and Lifecycle Stewardship**

* Own OT technology roadmaps aligned to business, regulatory, and investment priorities.
* Proactively manage technology obsolescence and lifecycle risk.
* Drive risk-based management of patching, upgrades, vulnerabilities, capacity, and technical debt.
* Establish standards for integration, automation, observability, and platform management.
* Enable trusted operational data, analytics, and AI capabilities.

**Portfolio Prioritization and Investment Leadership**

* Own OT demand, capacity, and prioritization across operations and capital programs.
* Lead transparent prioritization and resource trade-off decisions.
* Maintain credible operational and capital forecasts.
* Translate technology investments into measurable business outcomes.
* Ensure effective governance, intake, and decision-making processes.

**Enabling Capital Delivery and Operational Acceptance**

* Align OT resources to the highest-priority initiatives.
* Represent operational requirements throughout delivery and implementation.
* Ensure operational readiness before service acceptance.
* Identify and manage cross-program dependencies and risks.
* Enable smooth transition from project delivery to steady-state operations.

**Team Leadership, Capability and Culture**

* Lead and develop senior leaders across OT applications and infrastructure.
* Foster a culture of ownership, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Establish role clarity across internal teams, partners, and suppliers.
* Build workforce capability, succession plans, and organizational resilience.
* Ensure teams are trained and prepared to meet operational and compliance obligations.
* Strengthen collaboration across OT, IT&D, Operations, Cybersecurity, Engineering, and Capital Delivery.

**Stakeholder, Executive and Vendor Leadership**

* Build trusted partnerships with operational and business leaders.
* Provide clear, data-driven reporting to executives and governance forums.
* Lead strategic supplier performance, accountability, and risk management.
* Challenge decisions that increase operational risk or reduce delivery credibility.
* Act as the senior escalation point for critical operational and technology decisions.

### **Qualifications**

* Senior leadership experience within utility OT, critical infrastructure, or another highly regulated 24x7 operating environment.
* Demonstrated accountability for mission-critical services, operational risk, incident management, and service performance.
* Deep expertise in one or more OT domains (EMS, ADMS, DERMS, GMS, SCADA, OMS) with the ability to lead across a broader technology landscape.
* Experience leading multidisciplinary teams spanning applications, infrastructure, networks, integration, databases, and operational support.
* Strong understanding of cybersecurity, resilience, and regulatory frameworks, including NERC CIP and TSA requirements.
* Proven track record supporting large-scale transformation while maintaining operational stability.
* Experience managing strategic vendors, managed services, and system integrators.
* Strong financial, workforce, and portfolio management capabilities.
* Excellent executive communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or equivalent relevant experience.

Title: Shelter Manager
Description:
The Shelter Manager is responsible for the overall administrative and operational management of Animal Orphanage, ensuring the effective daily operation of the facility, supervision and administration of staff, financial and administrative coordination, customer service, regulatory compliance, and maintenance of the shelter's buildings, grounds, and vehicles.

This position serves as the senior operational manager of Animal Orphanage and provides leadership, direction, and oversight of shelter-wide operations. The Shelter Manager is responsible for coordinating the work of the Animal Care Manager and other shelter employees, establishing operational priorities, and ensuring that organizational policies and procedures are consistently followed.

The Shelter Manager has overall operational authority and final day-to-day decision-making responsibility, subject to the authority of the Board of Directors. The Shelter Manager reports directly to the President and Vice President of the Board of Directors.

JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Shelter Operations and Administration

* Oversees the day-to-day administrative and operational functions of the shelter to ensure efficient and consistent operations.
* Provides overall operational leadership and direction to the Animal Care Manager and other shelter employees.
* Establishes organizational priorities and coordinates responsibilities between the Animal Care Manager and other staff to ensure effective shelter operations.
* Develops, implements, and monitors operational procedures and policies for staff and volunteers in collaboration with the Animal Care Manager.
* Ensures shelter operations comply with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, licensing requirements, and organizational policies.
* Responsible for the completion and submission of required administrative paperwork and documentation necessary to maintain applicable licenses, certifications, and regulatory compliance.
* Maintains accurate and organized administrative records, files, and documentation.
* Ensures shelter management software and applicable administrative records are current and maintained, coordinating with the Animal Care Manager regarding animal-related records.
* Oversees website administration and ensures public-facing shelter information is accurate and current.
* Coordinates with other shelters, rescues, municipalities, and outside organizations as needed.
* Develops and maintains positive working relationships with Animal Control, law enforcement, local veterinarians, volunteers, foster families, and other stakeholders.
* Ensures the public receives accurate, consistent, and professional information regarding shelter services, policies, and operations.

Staff Supervision and Human Resources

* Responsible for the overall supervision and administration of shelter employees.
* Oversees employee recruitment, hiring coordination, onboarding, and orientation in collaboration with the Board President and Vice President.
* Develops and maintains staff schedules and assigns work responsibilities to ensure adequate operational coverage.
* Establishes overall staffing priorities and coordinates scheduling with the Animal Care Manager.
* Monitors staffing levels and evaluates operational needs to ensure appropriate allocation of personnel.
* Evaluates the need to fill vacant positions and recommends changes to staffing structure and allocated positions as needed.
* Oversees employee performance management, including evaluations, coaching, corrective action, and documentation.
* Addresses employee relations matters and works to maintain a professional, respectful, and productive workplace.
* Coordinates staff training and ensures employees receive appropriate instruction regarding workplace policies, safety procedures, and job responsibilities.
* Monitors attendance, timekeeping, and employee leave records.
* Coordinates payroll submissions and related documentation with the bookkeeper.
* Communicates staffing concerns, performance issues, and significant personnel matters to the Board President or Vice President as appropriate.
* Works collaboratively with the Animal Care Manager to address animal care staffing needs, training, performance, and scheduling.
* Establishes clear supervisory responsibilities and ensures employees receive consistent direction and understand reporting relationships.

Financial and Administrative Coordination

* Works directly with the bookkeeper to coordinate and maintain accurate administrative and financial records.
* Coordinates payroll submissions, mileage reimbursements, employee time records, and other documentation required for bookkeeping and payroll processing.
* Tracks and monitors routine shelter expenses and communicates financial or purchasing concerns to the Board President or Vice President.
* Coordinates purchasing and maintains appropriate inventory of administrative supplies, office equipment, and general facility supplies.
* Works with the Animal Care Manager to coordinate animal care supply and equipment purchasing needs.
* Ensures purchases are made in accordance with established budgets, purchasing procedures, and Board authorization requirements.
* Maintains accurate records of purchases, invoices, receipts, deposits, and other administrative transactions.
* Assists with budget preparation, expense tracking, and financial reporting as requested.
* Receives, processes, and records donations and other payments, including entering donation information into the organization's donor management platform.
* Prepares deposits and maintains accurate supporting documentation.
* Coordinates deposit preparation with the Animal Care Manager to ensure cash and checks are independently counted and deposit totals verified before submission.
* Does not assume responsibility for the Board Treasurer's financial oversight or the bookkeeper's accounting and reconciliation responsibilities.

Facility and Vehicle Maintenance

* Ensures the shelter facility, buildings, grounds, and vehicles are maintained in a safe, sanitary, and functional condition.
* Regularly inspects shelter property to identify needed repairs, maintenance, and safety improvements.
* Coordinates necessary maintenance, repairs, and service work for buildings, grounds, equipment, and the shelter-owned vehicle.
* Coordinates outside contractors and service providers as needed.
* Monitors facility maintenance needs and communicates significant repairs, expenses, or safety concerns to the Board President or Vice President.
* Maintains records of facility maintenance, repairs, and vehicle servicing.
* Ensures appropriate safety and sanitation standards are maintained throughout the facility in collaboration with the Animal Care Manager.
* Coordinates maintenance of equipment and supplies necessary for daily shelter operations.

Customer Service and Public Relations

* Oversees customer service standards and ensures inquiries from the public are handled professionally and in a timely manner.
* Addresses customer complaints, concerns, and escalated issues involving shelter operations and services.
* Ensures staff communicate shelter policies and procedures accurately and consistently.
* Oversees the administrative aspects of public inquiries, including adoption-related communications and follow-up.
* Works with the Animal Care Manager to ensure adoption applicants receive timely communication and accurate information.
* Supports positive relationships with municipal partners, community organizations, donors, volunteers, and the public.

Safety, Compliance, and Incident Reporting

Safety and Incident Reporting

* Ensures workplace safety policies and procedures are implemented and followed by all employees and volunteers throughout shelter operations.
* Identifies and addresses potential safety hazards involving employees, volunteers, visitors, animals, facilities, vehicles, and shelter operations.
* Ensures appropriate safety procedures are followed regarding hazardous materials, chemicals, equipment, and other workplace hazards.
* Completes and maintains administrative incident documentation as necessary.
* Oversees reporting and follow-up for operational incidents involving employees, volunteers, visitors, facilities, vehicles, and shelter operations, in coordination with the Animal Care Manager when animal care is involved.
* Ensures required incident reports are completed, appropriate notifications are made, and corrective or follow-up actions are addressed.
* Ensures significant workplace injuries, animal-related incidents, bites, escapes, safety concerns, regulatory issues, and operational emergencies are promptly communicated to the Board President or Vice President.
* Works collaboratively with the Animal Care Manager to investigate incidents, identify contributing factors, and implement appropriate corrective measures.

Cross-Training and Operational Coverage

* Develops and maintains working knowledge of the Animal Care Manager's essential responsibilities to provide operational coverage during absences, vacations, or other staffing needs.
* Cross-trains with the Animal Care Manager on essential animal care procedures, shelter operations, animal-related recordkeeping, and other responsibilities necessary to maintain continuity of operations.
* Provides reasonable assistance with animal care and other responsibilities outside the primary area of administrative and operational oversight when necessary to maintain shelter operations.
* Coordinates with the Animal Care Manager to ensure ongoing responsibilities, outstanding issues, and time-sensitive matters are communicated and addressed during periods of absence.
* When providing coverage, operates within established policies, procedures, and delegated authority. Veterinary and medical decisions must remain within the scope of appropriate veterinary direction and professional judgment.
* Retains overall operational authority and coordinates decisions requiring management oversight during periods when the Animal Care Manager is unavailable.
* Communicates significant decisions, operational concerns, and matters requiring additional authority to the Board President and Vice President.

Reporting and Board Communication

* Provides regular updates regarding shelter operations, staffing, administrative matters, facility needs, and significant operational concerns.
* Prepares and submits operational reports for monthly Board meetings.
* Serves as the primary management contact for routine operational communication with the Board President and Vice President.
* Communicates significant changes in staffing, operational needs, and facility conditions to the Board President and Vice President.
* Assists with the development and implementation of organizational policies, procedures, and operational improvements.
* Maintains appropriate confidentiality regarding employee, applicant, donor, financial, and organizational information.
* Other duties as assigned by the Board President and Vice President.

AUTHORITY AND REPORTING RELATIONSHIP

The Shelter Manager serves as the senior operational manager of Animal Orphanage and reports directly to the President and Vice President of the Board of Directors.

The Shelter Manager has overall responsibility for the daily operation of the shelter and final day-to-day decision-making authority regarding operational priorities, staffing and scheduling, administrative matters, customer service, facility operations, and coordination between departments, subject to established organizational policies, approved budgets, and the authority of the Board of Directors.

The Animal Care Manager reports directly to the Shelter Manager and has primary responsibility and decision-making authority over daily animal care operations and the direction of animal care staff within established policies and veterinary guidance.

The Shelter Manager is responsible for coordinating the work of both management positions, resolving operational disagreements, and ensuring organizational priorities are met. This authority does not eliminate the Animal Care Manager's responsibility or professional judgment regarding animal welfare and daily animal care practices. Veterinary medical decisions must remain consistent with veterinary direction.

Significant animal welfare, safety, regulatory, personnel, financial, or other organizational concerns must be elevated to the Board President or Vice President as appropriate. The Board retains authority over organizational governance, policies, budgets, and major personnel decisions.

REQUIRED SKILLS

Computer Skills: Proficiency with personal computers, word processing, spreadsheets, email, website administration, shelter management software, and related programs.

Judgment and Decision Making: Ability to evaluate operational needs, establish priorities, anticipate potential problems, and make sound decisions within the scope of assigned responsibilities.

Interpersonal Relationships: Ability to develop and maintain cooperative and professional relationships with employees, board members, volunteers, vendors, municipal representatives, and other organizations.

You will lead a global team of product managers, product owners, and developers while collaborating closely with portfolio management, sales, operations, finance, and regional business leaders. Combining strategic business leadership, product management excellence, and strong commercial acumen, you will act as a chief business developer who navigates complex stakeholder expectations to deliver sustainable growth and long-term customer value.

**Key Responsibilities**

Portfolio Strategy & Business Leadership

* Drive and execute the long-term multi-year growth strategy for the RUGGEDCOM portfolio, aligned with Siemens business objectives.
* Oversee overall portfolio performance, including revenue growth, profitability, market share, and return on investment.
* Drive accountability for annual strategy development, operating plans, and portfolio investment decisions.
* Identify and pursue growth opportunities through new markets, applications, technologies, partnerships, and acquisitions.
* Product Lifecycle Management
* Oversee end-to-end product lifecycle management—spanning requirement definition, R&D alignment, rigorous testing, and commercial release.
* Establish and maintain market-leading product roadmaps informed by customer needs, technology trends, and competitive analysis.
* Align investments and resources across the portfolio to maximize business value and customer impact based on long-term strategy.
* Drive product launch excellence, lifecycle optimization, and effective management of product transitions, obsolescence planning, and portfolio rationalization.
* Customer and Market Leadership
* Serve as the executive voice of the customer, building strategic relationships with key utilities, EPCs, system integrators, channel partners, and industry stakeholders.
* Represent RUGGEDCOM at executive customer engagements, industry forums, and strategic business reviews.
* Translate market intelligence, competitive dynamics, and emerging technologies into actionable portfolio opportunities.
* Cross-Executive & Operational Leadership
* Build, coach, and develop a high-performing, diverse global organization.
* Influence and partner with R&D leadership to align product development priorities with business objectives.
* Collaborate with sales, marketing, operations, and supply chain teams to optimize product availability, cost competitiveness, lifecycle sustainability, and market penetration.
* Develop business cases and investment proposals, managing key portfolio KPIs (revenue, margin, growth, market share, product vitality, and customer satisfaction) while ensuring optimized product costing.

  

**Required Qualifications**

* Master’s degree preferred (minimum Bachelor's) in Engineering, Computer Science, Business, or a related discipline.
* 15+ years of experience in industrial technology, networking, telecommunications, automation, software, or adjacent domains, anchored by expertise in communications infrastructure, automation systems, or cybersecurity.
* 10+ years of leadership experience spanning Product Management, Product Lifecycle Management, Portfolio Management, or General Management.
* Proven track record of leading product portfolios to drive sustained business growth across multi-market environments.
* Expertise in shaping winning product strategies and driving high-impact technology roadmaps from conception to market success.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and align executive stakeholders.
* Strong financial and business acumen.

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Demonstrated experience navigating harsh operational technology (OT) environments where rugged communications infrastructure is foundational.
* Deep understanding of the competitive landscape within industrial networking and customer challenges.
* Experience supporting critical infrastructure industries including utilities, transportation, mining, oil & gas, and defense.
* Knowledge of utility communications, IEC 61850, cybersecurity, industrial Ethernet, or mission-critical networking technologies.
* Track record of successfully leading organizational transformation and portfolio modernization initiatives.
* Strategic Vision & Product Leadership: Shaping long-term product strategies, technology roadmaps, and portfolio growth.
* People Leadership & Talent Development: Building, coaching, and inspiring high-performing global teams.
* Executive Presence & Collaboration: Navigating complex stakeholder networks and driving cross-functional alignment.
* Commercial Acumen & Customer Focus: Maximizing business value, market impact, and customer-centric innovation.
* Change Leadership & Results Orientation: Steering transformations and consistently delivering high-stakes outcomes.

  

**Success Measures (First 24 Months)**

* Strengthen customer engagement and market leadership in critical infrastructure segments.
* Deliver above-market portfolio growth and increased profitability.
* Strengthen and scale the PLM organization to power future growth by streamlining portfolio lifecycles and optimizing resource allocation.
* Accelerate new product introductions and portfolio modernization.

Title: Senior Portfolio & Program Manager, Operational Technology & Controls
Description:
**Who are we?**
Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.
  
  
A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.
  
  
A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.
  
  
**Job Summary**
The Senior Portfolio & Program Manager, Operational Technology & Controls is responsible for the integrated portfolio of Operational Technology & Engineering (OT&E) initiatives across controls, central monitoring, OT infrastructure, cybersecurity, data, and automation, ensuring programs are sequenced, governed, funded, and transitioned to operations as one connected roadmap rather than as separate projects.
  
  
This role combines disciplined portfolio and program management with proven, hands-on expertise in industrial controls and operational technology, including how controls systems integrate across critical facilities. It does not replace technical owners: engineering owns design, architecture, and engineering acceptance, while this role owns portfolio governance, integration, and transition to operations, and recommends sequencing, funding, and prioritization decisions to leadership. This position collaborates with engineering, operations, cybersecurity, IT, network, architecture, finance, procurement, vendors, system integrators, and regional teams across Global Operations Excellence to deliver key initiatives such as GMCC and central SCADA, and to strengthen the reliability, security, and supportability of Equinix’s critical facilities.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Maintain a single, current view of all OT&E initiatives, including scope, funding, dependencies, risk, and expected value
* Run intake, scoring, and prioritization of new work against strategy, architectural standards, and capacity
* Lead quarterly and annual planning, roadmap development, and investment cases, partnering with Finance on forecasting and variance reporting
* Lead multi-team programs end to end, including integrated plans, critical paths, and phased global rollouts to site teams
* Define and enforce stage gates and readiness criteria (design, security review, pilot, production)
* Ensure programs conform to approved architecture and engineering standards, working closely with architecture and review boards
* Run program governance, including steering committees, status cadences, RAID logs, and decision records
* Creates clarity from complexity by turning strategy, competing priorities, and incomplete information into an executable roadmap
* Balances pace, cost, technical quality, cybersecurity, and long-term supportability in program decisions
* Translate technical detail into executive-ready narratives, dashboards, and decision requests
* Manage vendor and integrator engagements, including SOWs, deliverables, and performance
* Track benefits realization and report whether delivered programs achieved their intended outcomes.

**Qualifications**

* Typically, 10+ years in program or portfolio management, including 5+ years leading complex technical programs
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, technology, or a related field is desired.
* Nice to Have: PMP or PMI certification, P.Eng., Lean, or Agile certification; ITIL Foundation or ServiceNow experience
* Experience managing concurrent programs with shared dependencies and constrained resources
* Proven, hands-on expertise in industrial controls and operational technology within data centre or critical facilities environments
* Brings solid controls and OT expertise to engage engineers as a credible peer, challenge plans, and recognize material technical dependencies, while respecting engineering as the technical authority
* Technical knowledge of Building Management Systems (BMS), power monitoring, SCADA, telemetry, and OT/IT network segmentation, including how these systems integrate, sufficient to challenge estimates and technical plans and spot risk
* Strong financial acumen, including budget ownership and business case development
* Proven ability to influence senior leaders and drive decisions without direct authority
* Experience with both stage-gate and agile delivery approaches
* Excellent facilitation, negotiation, written communication, and executive presentation skills, able to influence in a global, matrixed environment without direct authority

Title: Managing Director, Services
Description:

**Ready to discover the possibilities that live in technology?**

  

**Come Join Us!**

**Street-Smart** **-** ***Thriving in Dynamic Times***

We are flexible and resilient in a fast-changing environment. We continuously innovate and drive constructive change while keeping a focus on the "big picture." We exercise sound business judgment in making high-quality decisions in a timely and cost-effective manner. We are highly creative and can dig deep within ourselves to find positive solutions to different problems.

**Juice -** ***The "Stuff" it takes to be a Needle Mover***

We get things done and drive results. We lead without a title, empowering others through a can-do attitude. We look forward to the goal, mentally mapping out every checkpoint on the pathway to success, and visualizing what the final destination looks and feels like.

**Teamwork -** ***Humble, Hungry and Smart***

We are humble individuals who understand how our job impacts the company's mission. We treat others with respect, admit mistakes, give credit where it's due and demonstrate transparency. We "bring the weather" by exhibiting positive leadership and solution-focused thinking. We hug people in their trials, struggles, and failures – not just their success. We appreciate the individuality of the people around us.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

Under the direction of the General Manager and Account Executive and in close partnership with the Strategic Account Managers, the Managing Director, Services is responsible for accelerating services growth across the FSG client base. This leader identifies, shapes, and advances consulting-led opportunities spanning Management Consulting and IT Services, including managed services and capabilities across Security, Data and Analytics, Cloud, Networking, Infrastructure, and adjacent technology domains. The role brings a management consulting approach to client discovery, executive alignment, solution development, pursuit leadership, and commercial strategy, connecting client business priorities to measurable outcomes and executable services engagements. This is a services sales leadership role, not an account ownership or day-to-day delivery management position. Account Executive and Strategic Account Managers retain account ownership, while this role leads the services strategy and selling motion in partnership with them.

**SUMMARY OF ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:**

**Services Sales Strategy & Revenue Growth**

* Develop and execute account-level services growth strategies in partnership with the General Manager, Account Executives, and Strategic Account Managers.

* Identify, qualify, shape, and advance Management Consulting and IT Services opportunities within existing clients and selected prospects.

* Create demand by connecting client business priorities, operational challenges, risk exposure, and transformation goals to relevant consulting and technology services.

* Lead complex, multi-workstream services pursuits from early discovery through proposal, negotiation, and close.

* Build, maintain, and forecast a qualified services pipeline with clear next steps, decision criteria, competitive positioning, and close plans.

* Meet or exceed assigned bookings, revenue, gross profit, and pipeline objectives.

**Executive Client Engagement & Consultative Selling**

* Build trusted relationships with senior business and technology leaders, including C-suite executives, transformation leaders, security leaders, data leaders, infrastructure leaders, and procurement stakeholders.

* Lead executive discovery sessions and working meetings to clarify business problems, desired outcomes, priorities, constraints, and investment rationale.

* Use hypothesis-driven, outcome-oriented consulting techniques to frame opportunities and build consensus across business and technology stakeholders.

* Translate complex client needs into clear problem statements, value propositions, roadmaps, and services recommendations.

* Position Trace3 as a long-term advisory and services partner rather than a transactional technology provider.

**Management Consulting & IT Services Portfolio Leadership**

* Drive sales across Management Consulting offerings such as strategy, operating model, organizational change, program leadership, maturity assessments, roadmaps, governance, and transformation planning.

* Drive sales across IT Services, including managed services and project-based services in Security, Data and Analytics, Cloud, Networking, Infrastructure, and related technology domains.

* Partner with consulting, managed services, engineering, architecture, delivery, and domain leaders to assemble integrated solutions across multiple practices.

* Identify opportunities to expand from advisory work into implementation and managed services, and from technical engagements into broader consulting relationships.

* Maintain sufficient knowledge of the services portfolio, delivery models, commercial constructs, and relevant partner capabilities to credibly lead executive sales conversations.

**Pursuit Leadership, Solution Development & Commercial Strategy**

* Orchestrate pursuit teams, establish win strategy, define roles, and maintain momentum across complex sales cycles.

* Lead the development of proposals, statements of work, presentations, business cases, and executive-level recommendations in collaboration with solution and delivery leaders.

* Ensure proposed scope, assumptions, outcomes, staffing model, pricing, timeline, and delivery approach are aligned before client commitment.

* Partner with account leadership, legal, finance, operations, and delivery teams on pricing, risk review, contracting, and negotiation.

* Conduct effective handoffs to delivery leadership while preserving client context, intended outcomes, commercial commitments, and expansion opportunities.

**Account Planning & Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* Embed a services strategy into priority account plans, including whitespace analysis, stakeholder mapping, relationship development, and pursuit sequencing.

* Partner with Account Executives and Strategic Account Managers to coordinate client messaging, coverage, opportunity ownership, and executive engagement.

* Collaborate with marketing and practice leaders on campaigns, events, thought leadership, and market-facing programs that generate services demand.

* Engage strategic technology and services partners when their capabilities strengthen the client solution and improve the probability of winning.

* Escalate commercial, resourcing, solution, or delivery risks early and drive cross-functional resolution.

**Performance Management & Business Reporting**

* Maintain accurate opportunity data, pipeline stages, forecasts, activity, and pursuit plans in the company CRM and related operating tools.

* Report services pipeline, bookings, revenue outlook, pursuit health, conversion rates, and account penetration to leadership.

* Use win/loss analysis, client feedback, delivery outcomes, and market intelligence to improve positioning and sales execution.

* Provide visibility into capability gaps, investment needs, competitive threats, and emerging client demand.

**TYPICAL ALLOCATION OF RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Services Strategy, Opportunity Identification & Account Planning (25%)

* Executive Client Engagement & Consultative Discovery (25%)

* Pursuit Leadership, Solution Development & Commercial Strategy (25%)

* Pipeline Management, Forecasting & Performance Reporting (15%)

Title: Senior Program Manager, Strategy and Expansion, MEATR DSP Strategy, Planning and Expansion
Description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Customers want what they need in minutes, not days. Join Amazon's Last Mile team in the Middle East, Africa and Turkey to shape how our fastest delivery services, including Amazon Now and Amazon Rush, grow and run for customers, delivery associates, Delivery Service Partners (DSPs) and Amazon.  
  
As Senior Program Manager, you will own and lead the strategic programmes that set how our Speed last mile network runs across the region. At the core is flexible capacity: designing models that let DSP capacity move up and down with demand, setting how they fit into annual and weekly planning, and getting Operations, Finance, People teams and DSP partners behind them. Your portfolio may also cover partner commercials, compliance and training, and it will change as priorities change.  
  
Many problems won't arrive well defined. You will frame them, find the ones worth solving, align senior stakeholders on a path forward and build mechanisms that make the answers scale across countries. You will also help shape the team's wider strategy and roadmap.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* Set the strategy: own the multi-year capacity and growth plan for Quick Commerce and Speed, and the region's input to annual planning.
* Plan capacity: within the regional plan, build short, mid and long range plans that match DSP and delivery associate supply to demand by hour, day and season.
* Build flexible capacity: design, launch and scale flexible models alongside the fixed DSP network, with the operating, commercial and compliance framework to run them.
* Grow the channel: launch new cities, stores and countries with capacity ready before go-live.
* Improve efficiency: raise utilisation and lower cost per delivery without moving cost onto DSPs or associates.
* Build partner economics: shape DSP commercial models with Finance that work at every volume level, and lead the trade-off decisions.
* Look after delivery associates: design fair, safe, compliant schedules and lead the regional response to labour rule changes.
* Align and lead change: bring Operations, Finance, People, Legal, Tech and DSPs behind one plan, and run readiness and approvals.
* Build mechanisms: set planning tool requirements with Tech, and the metrics, guardrails and reviews that run the channel, using automation and AI.
* Lead and write: influence senior leaders, mentor PMs and analysts, and write documents that drive decisions.

  
A day in the life  
You start with yesterday's Quick Commerce and Speed performance: where capacity matched demand, where routes ran short or associates sat idle, and what it cost. Mid-morning, you join the weekly planning review to agree where flexible capacity steps in next week. You then meet a DSP owner to test a new flexible model against their margin and their associates' hours. After lunch, you work with Finance and Legal on the case for scaling it to a second country. You end the day writing for senior leaders: what the pilot showed, what you recommend and what you need from them.  
  
About the team  
This is a new role reporting to the Senior Manager, Strategy and Expansion, MEATr DSP. Quick Commerce and Speed, including Amazon Now and Amazon Rush, are delivered by DSPs, and flexible capacity is a lead theme in the region's 2027 plan. You will own Speed capacity and flexible capacity programmes across the region, planning inside the regional capacity plan and working with the Network Optimisation team, who own rate cards. You will mentor PMs and analysts and write planning papers reviewed at Director and VP level.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* 2+ years of program or project management experience
* Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
* Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
* Experience owning program strategy, end-to-end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* 2+ years of driving process improvements experience
* Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field

Title: Senior Director, Software & Services Strategy
Description:
**Job Description**
===================

The Senior Director, Software & Services Strategy will report directly to the VP, Strategy, Power and serve as the enterprise strategist and business architect for the convergence of software, controls, industrial data, artificial intelligence, and lifecycle services across the Power Segment.

The role will help Power evolve from a model centered primarily on equipment control, software products, and event-based service delivery toward an integrated growth system that uses proprietary industrial context, trusted intelligence, validated action, and service execution to improve customer availability, reliability, productivity, operating economics, and lifecycle value.

This leader will not replace the operating accountability of Services or Software & Controls Solutions. Instead, the leader will own the strategic seams between them: the integrated thesis, value-pool choices, business architecture, new commercial and contract models, ecosystem strategy, cross-business governance, and incubation of the first scalable integrated offers.

  
  

**Why the Role Is Needed**
==========================

Power’s Services business represents a foundational long-term profit pool. Software & Controls Solutions is smaller today from a P&L perspective but has significant growth ambitions and provides capabilities that can reshape the future economics and differentiation of Services. The critical strategic question is therefore broader than how to grow software as a standalone business.

* The most important future customer outcomes span organizational boundaries and cannot be captured by Services, Software & Controls Solutions, Engineering, or Digital Technology acting independently.

* Industrial software firms, systems integrators, hyperscalers, OEMs, and AI-native entrants are increasingly competing to own the customer’s data context, workflow layer, decision interface, and transformation agenda.

* GE Vernova’s differentiated starting point is its installed base, controls authority, equipment and fleet knowledge, service history, customer relationships, and ability to translate insight into safe, validated action.

* Without coordinated leadership, fragmented investment, unclear commercial credit, competing roadmaps, and slow cross-business decisions could prevent Power from converting those assets into durable growth.

* The role creates a single point of accountability for translating the strategy into a portfolio of customer-backed ventures and scalable operating-model choices.

  
  

**Mission**
===========

**Build the strategy, operating model, partnerships, commercial architecture, and transformation portfolio required for Software, Controls, AI, Industrial Data, and Services to operate as one integrated growth system.**

  
  

**Strategic Outcomes**
======================

* Protect and expand the lifecycle Services franchise by anticipating digital disintermediation and embedding differentiated software and AI capabilities into customer value delivery.

* Create recurring, software-enabled, managed-service, and outcome-based revenue streams without unintentionally eroding attractive service-event economics.

* Move Power’s customer value proposition from monitoring and insight toward prevention, optimization, trusted execution, and accountable outcomes.

* Increase the strategic and commercial integration of Services and Software & Controls Solutions while preserving the capabilities, talent, architecture, and operating cadence required for software success.

* Focus investment on defensible capabilities rooted in industrial context, controls-aware decisioning, cybersecure action, service integration, and outcome accountability.

* Build credible options for a future Software & Services growth platform if market evidence and economics support that evolution.

  
  

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

**1. Integrated Strategy and Portfolio Leadership**
---------------------------------------------------

* Develop and maintain the three-to-five-year Software, AI, Controls, Industrial Data, and Services transformation strategy for Power.

* Translate customer value pools and competitive threats into clear where-to-play, how-to-win, build-buy-partner, and investment choices.

* Maintain an integrated portfolio across near-term franchise protection, scalable growth, and longer-horizon autonomous operations and enterprise optimization.

* Establish decision criteria for which capabilities Power should own, control, influence through partnership, or treat as commodity infrastructure.

**2. Services and SCS Bridge**
------------------------------

* Create shared strategic priorities and a coherent business architecture across Services and Software & Controls Solutions.

* Resolve or escalate cross-business issues involving offer ownership, roadmap dependencies, commercial credit, customer access, data rights, investment responsibility, and value attribution.

* Ensure integrated offers use the Services channel, operating expertise, and execution capability while protecting software product discipline, talent, release cadence, and platform integrity.

* Design clear activation and transfer points so proven ventures can scale through the appropriate operating business.

**3. New Offers, Commercial Models, and Contracts**
---------------------------------------------------

* Lead definition of integrated offer archetypes such as Intelligent CSA, Availability-as-a-Service, autonomous O&M enablement, managed fleet intelligence, and fleet performance partnerships.

* Design pricing, packaging, subscription, event-based, shared-savings, performance-incentive, and outcome-based commercial models.

* Partner with Finance, Legal, Risk, Services, and Engineering to develop disciplined guardrails for warranties, guarantees, data use, cybersecurity, baselines, and outcome underwriting.

* Create the economics and incentive mechanisms required to embed software within Services contracts and commercial motions.

**4. Customer Co-Creation and Venture Incubation**
--------------------------------------------------

* Select and engage lighthouse customers with the strategic relevance, data access, executive sponsorship, and willingness to co-develop new operating and commercial models.

* Convert pilots into scalable ventures with a defined customer outcome, accountable business owner, technical owner, value baseline, scale gate, and receiving organization.

* Ensure customer finance and operating teams validate value before broad investment and scale.

* Build repeatable approaches for moving from asset-level use cases to plant, fleet, and enterprise applications.

**5. Platform, Ecosystem, and Corporate Development Strategy**
--------------------------------------------------------------

* Define the industrial context and interoperability principles connecting controls, asset models, service history, knowledge graphs, edge and cloud deployment, applications, and customer workflows.

* Lead strategic assessment of technology partners, hyperscalers, industrial software firms, systems integrators, AI-native entrants, and acquisition targets.

* Develop build-buy-partner recommendations based on strategic control, differentiation, speed, economics, talent, integration risk, and customer access.

* Protect GE Vernova’s industrial intellectual property, customer position, portability, data rights, and margin while making effective use of external platforms.

  
  

**Operating Model and Governance**
==================================

* Reports directly to the VP, Strategy, Power.

* Works through formal co-sponsorship and standing governance with Services and Software & Controls Solutions leadership.

* Chairs or leads the working-level transformation portfolio process and prepares decisions for Power leadership.

* Uses explicit venture gates: customer problem validated, value baseline approved, technical feasibility demonstrated, commercial model tested, scale economics confirmed, and receiving organization agreed.

* Operates with a ring-fenced but disciplined transformation investment pool for cross-business pilots and shared capabilities.

* Does not build a large parallel delivery organization. Product delivery and service execution remain with the accountable operating businesses.

  
  

**Candidate Profile**
=====================

The ideal candidate is a hybrid strategist, operator, and business builder who can connect industrial technology to customer and financial outcomes. The person must be credible with software and technical leaders, Services operators, commercial teams, and senior executives, while remaining focused on enterprise value rather than the success of any single organizational silo.

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* Significant relevant experience in strategy, software, industrial technology, lifecycle services, digital transformation, or business building, with demonstrated leadership in complex global organizations.

* Demonstrated ability to shape and execute strategies spanning multiple P&Ls, functions, technologies, and customer buying centers.

* Strong understanding of industrial or mission-critical environments where reliability, safety, cybersecurity, and installed-base economics matter.

* Experience translating customer outcomes into value propositions, commercial models, investment cases, and executable transformation portfolios.

* Demonstrated skill in executive communication, influence without direct authority, conflict resolution, and enterprise decision making.

* Experience evaluating partnerships, ecosystems, strategic investments, or M&A opportunities.

* Ability to lead a small senior team and mobilize broader cross-functional venture squads.

Title: Guest Experience Manager

**Department:** Guest Services  
**Reports To:** Director of Guest Services  
**Status:** Exempt, Full-Time  
**Supervises:** Guest Services Agents and Bellstaff during assigned shifts; Gift Shop operations  
**Location:** Santa Monica, California  
**Salary Range:** 73K

**Position Summary**

The Guest Experience Manager is responsible for enhancing guest satisfaction, strengthening Shore Hotel's online reputation, overseeing concierge services and special guest experiences, and managing Gift Shop operations. The position also provides operational leadership and Manager on Duty (MOD) coverage, ensuring consistent service standards and a personalized guest experience.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on hospitality professional with strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and organizational skills.

**Essential Duties & Responsibilities**

**1. Leadership & Operations**

* Serve as Manager on Duty (MOD) and provide Front Desk leadership coverage, including weekends, holidays, and other shifts as business needs require.
* Support Front Desk operations during high-volume periods, staffing shortages, and management absences.
* Supervise and coach Guest Services Agents and Bell staff during assigned shifts, ensuring consistent service standards.
* Support the Guest Services Manager with onboarding, training, and operational initiatives as needed.
* Conduct service observations, identify operational deficiencies, and implement corrective actions.
* Ensure compliance with hotel SOPs, cash handling, credit policies, guest confidentiality, and safety procedures.
* Coordinate with Housekeeping, Engineering, Reservations, Valet, and other departments to ensure seamless operations.
* Respond to guest emergencies, incidents, and operational disruptions in accordance with established procedures.
* Maintain proficiency in Opera Cloud and other hotel operating systems.

**2. Reputation Management**

* Oversee guest reviews across TripAdvisor, Google, and major booking platforms, with primary emphasis on TripAdvisor performance and ranking.
* Monitor and respond to guest reviews promptly, ensuring personalized, professional communication.
* Develop initiatives to improve guest satisfaction, online reputation, and authentic guest engagement.
* Analyze review trends, recurring complaints, and service deficiencies, coordinating improvements with department leaders.
* Track guest satisfaction scores, ratings, rankings, review volume, and response timeliness.
* Recognize employees mentioned positively in reviews and coach teams on service improvement opportunities.
* Provide monthly reputation performance updates and recommendations to the Director of Guest Services.

**3. Guest Experience**

* Oversee the guest journey, including pre-arrival preparation, personalized recognition, in-house engagement, and post-stay follow-up.
* Develop and maintain a curated network of trusted restaurants, tours, attractions, transportation providers, and local experiences.
* Train Front Desk Agents on concierge services, local recommendations, and personalized guest engagement.
* Manage special-occasion programs, VIP recognition, repeat guest preferences, and personalized amenities.
* Proactively engage with guests to anticipate needs and identify opportunities to enhance their stays.
* Manage escalated guest concerns and service recoveries through resolution, including follow-up and documentation.
* Exercise discretion in resolving guest issues within approved service recovery guidelines.
* Monitor guest satisfaction trends, identify service gaps, and implement approved improvements.
* Collaborate with all departments to ensure a seamless, memorable guest experience.

**4. Gift Shop Management**

* Oversee daily Gift Shop operations, merchandising, sales procedures, and overall presentation.
* Manage inventory, purchasing, vendor relationships, and product replenishment.
* Conduct inventory counts, reconcile variances, and implement shrinkage prevention measures.
* Maintain competitive pricing, appealing displays, and appropriate Shore Hotel-branded merchandise.
* Monitor sales performance, expenses, and profitability.

Title: Senior Operations Manager
Description:
**ROLE SUMMARY**

The Senior Operations Manager is responsible for overseeing the operational performance of a large cluster or multiple territories within the assigned retail network. The role ensures best-in-class store execution, operational consistency, and commercial performance while driving elevated customer experience and strong team development. This position acts as the key operational bridge between Area Managers, Store Managers, and the Operations Director, ensuring flawless delivery of retail standards, business strategies, and cross-functional initiatives.

**ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES**

Store Operations Leadership

* Lead and support Area Managers and Store Managers to ensure consistent daily store execution across all assigned territories.
* Ensure all stores follow retail standards, operational SOPs, safety protocols, and compliance expectations.
* Own territory operational KPIs including revenue, conversion, ATV, UPT, productivity, shrinkage, and customer service results.
* Perform structured store visits with follow-up actions and continuous performance tracking.

Commercial & Business Performance

* Drive territory commercial performance, overseeing a portfolio generating AED 1.2M–3M per area depending on store mix.
* Lead weekly and monthly business reviews with Area Managers and Store Managers to analyze sales trends, identify gaps, and build action plans.
* Ensure effective execution of promotions, campaigns, and seasonal launches in line with Marketing, VM, and Merchandising teams.
* Build annual store performance forecasts and support budgeting with Operations Director.

Merchandising, Allocation & Inventory

* Work closely with Merchandising and Allocation teams to ensure product availability, replenishment, and assortment alignment across all stores.
* Provide structured feedback on stock gaps, assortment performance, customer buying trends, and SKU productivity.
* Support Area Managers in ensuring stores execute brand visual standards and floor-set requirements.

People & Performance Management

* Lead and coach a team of Area Managers, supporting their development, performance management, and succession planning.
* Partner with HR to build strong frontline capabilities, training pathways, and leadership pipelines.
* Ensure stores are properly staffed, schedules optimized, and labor aligned with productivity targets.
* Drive a high-performance and customer-first culture across the territory.

Process Excellence & Compliance

* Monitor store compliance across operational checklists, LP guidelines, audit standards, and health & safety requirements.
* Lead operational improvement initiatives, driving consistency and efficiency across all districts.
* Support roll-out of new retail systems, tools, and processes, ensuring adoption by store teams.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

* Work closely with Operations, Merchandising, VM, Marketing, HR, and Finance to deliver integrated commercial and operational plans.
* Represent Operations in brand, business, and strategic discussions when delegated by the Operations Director.
* Act as escalation point for Area Managers, resolving operational issues and coordinating with relevant departments.

**ROLE REQUIREMENTS**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, Retail Management, Operations, or a related field (required), master’s degree preferred.
* Relevant certifications in Lean Six Sigma, Retail Operations, or Project Management are an advantage.
* 7–10 years of experience in large-format or specialty retail, with at least 3–5 years in multi-store leadership (Area/Cluster Manager level).
* Proven experience managing international retail brands, preferably within the sports, fashion, or lifestyle sectors.
* Strong P&L understanding, commercial acumen, and KPI-driven performance management.
* Experience managing high-volume retail territories is preferred.
* Strong expertise in customer experience, inventory management, stock flow, and visual merchandising.
* Proven capabilities in people leadership, coaching, operational strategy, retail compliance, and audit standards.
* Strong cross-functional communication, stakeholder management, and project execution skills.

Title: Events Operations Manager
Description:

* Degree in Events Management, Sports Management, Business, Marketing or a related field (equivalent relevant experience may be considered)

* Experience managing senior stakeholders, preferably including sports authorities, schools or public-sector organisations

**Knowledge and skills**
